headline: Tech stocks took a hit last night as Microsoft fell hard on AI cost fears, while the ASX held steady with energy and diversified ETFs leading the local gains today.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 3.17% last night — a significant fall driven by investor jitters after earnings. The market is worried about the enormous cost of Microsoft's AI buildout, with analysts questioning whether returns will justify the spending. IBD noted the stock is trying to 'retake a key level' after recent sell-off pressure.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two fell nearly 3% last night. There's no major company-specific catalyst — the broader tech/NASDAQ sell-off dragged it down. GTA 6 hype remains high (fans literally broke into Rockstar's office looking for info), but excitement alone isn't moving the stock right now.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped 1.83% at today's close. Lithium sentiment is still uncertain despite Citi turning bullish on the broader lithium price outlook and raising targets for Chinese producers. Investors remain cautious on Australian lithium stocks until a sustained price recovery shows up in earnings.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL had a solid session today, up 1.75%. Oil prices surged last night (WTI crude up 2.73% to $96.32/barrel) on supply fears tied to the Iran conflict disrupting the IEA's market outlook. The IEA is now warning of critically low stockpiles before peak summer demand — that's a strong tailwind for energy stocks.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.91% today — a modest positive session for the AI ETF. The overall AI investment theme remains strong, though today's gains were tempered by the broader tech weakness dragging on US-listed AI names.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG slipped 0.76% last night. Sentiment is cautious after a prominent tech commentator (M.G. Siegler) argued Google is falling behind OpenAI and Anthropic in the AI race, and that strategic missteps could be 'company-destroying.' Long-term revenue growth story remains intact, but the short-term AI narrative is favouring rivals.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.66% today — a quiet but positive session. As a broadly diversified fund, it benefited from strength in local energy and US market ETF components, with the ASX broadly stable.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.46% at today's ASX close, reflecting the pricing lag from last night's US session. The NASDAQ fell 0.89% last night, so today's ASX price likely already baked in some of that softness — tonight's US open will be the real test.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was essentially flat today, dipping just 0.16%. Emerging markets are in a holding pattern — no major catalyst. The slight Aussie dollar softness (AUD/USD down 0.44% to 0.7133) provides a minor tailwind for unhedged overseas exposure.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Sharp drop last night — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 3.17% last night, one of the biggest single-day drops in your portfolio. The sell-off is linked to ongoing concerns about the massive cost of its AI investments. IBD says the stock is trying to hold a key technical level. No fundamental reason to sell — Microsoft's AI strategy is credible — but expect volatility this week as the market digests earnings.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil spiking — strong tailwind
watch_today.detail: WTI crude hit $96.32/barrel last night, up 2.73%, driven by the Iran conflict upending global oil supply forecasts. The IEA is warning of critically low stockpiles before peak summer demand, and Deutsche Bank has raised its Brent crude target to $109. This is a direct tailwind for your FUEL.AX energy ETF. Worth considering adding if you want more energy exposure.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium slowly turning — watch closely
watch_today.detail: Pilbara slipped 1.83% today, but there are green shoots in the background: Citi has turned bullish on lithium prices, raising targets for major Chinese lithium producers Ganfeng and Tianqi. Motley Fool noted PLS is up 473% in a year — it's had a big run. Hold your position but watch for any price recovery catalyst before adding more.

watch_today.title: GOOG: AI narrative risk building
watch_today.detail: GOOG slipped 0.76% last night and the commentary is getting louder that Google is losing the AI race to OpenAI and Anthropic. Analyst M.G. Siegler called the shift to standalone AI apps 'challenging' for Google and warned of 'company-destroying' strategic missteps. On the positive side, Google's AI infrastructure spending is a boon for chipmakers like Broadcom. Keep a close eye this week — your GOOG position is still up 23% overall.

watch_today.title: Trump's new AI executive order — voluntary, not binding
watch_today.detail: The Trump administration has signed an executive order creating a voluntary 'pre-check' regime for frontier AI models from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Crucially, it's voluntary — not regulation. Critics say it won't be enough to manage risks or keep up with China. For your GXAI.AX and GOOG holdings, less regulation generally means fewer barriers to AI deployment, which is a mild positive.

watch_today.title: RBA rate path — economy slowing, cuts closer?
watch_today.detail: Australia's GDP is growing at just 2.5% annually and showing signs of slowing further. Analysts say the stalling economy could actually stop the RBA (Reserve Bank) from lifting rates any higher — and may even bring cuts forward. That's generally good for growth assets like shares and ETFs. Watch for any RBA commentary this week.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street was a soft session — both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ finished lower, dragged down mainly by big tech. Microsoft's continued post-earnings slide and broader AI cost concerns weighed on sentiment. Oil was the standout, jumping 2.73% on Middle East supply fears. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly against the USD. ASX 200 data wasn't available at close today.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — fell 0.74% as tech weakness spread across the market.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session — down 0.89%, led lower by Microsoft and the broader tech sector.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Surged 2.73% on Iran-related supply disruption fears and IEA warnings of low stockpiles.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Slight dip — still at historically elevated levels.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar slipped slightly — means your US holdings are worth a touch more in AUD terms.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Australia's economy showing signs of strain — GDP growth has slowed to 2.5% annually, and multiple analysts are warning it could get worse. That's shaping the conversation around interest rates and the federal budget.

stories.title: Australia's economy growing at just 2.5% — slowdown beginning
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's annual economic growth rate has slowed to 2.5% and appears to be losing steam. A slower economy generally means less consumer spending and business confidence — not great news. But for interest rates, it could actually be good: the Reserve Bank is less likely to hike rates further if the economy is already cooling. That's a potential positive for mortgage holders and growth investments.

stories.title: Stalling economy could stop further RBA rate hikes
stories.why_it_matters: Analysts are now saying the weak growth numbers could be enough to halt any further Reserve Bank interest rate rises. If the RBA holds or cuts, that's relief for everyone with a mortgage and a positive signal for shares. Some economists are even floating the possibility of rate cuts later in 2026 if conditions keep deteriorating.

stories.title: 'Worrying' growth slowdown may worsen as RBA decisions and war bite
stories.why_it_matters: AAP reports the slowdown could worsen, with two key pressures: the RBA's past rate hikes are still working their way through the economy (taking time to bite), and the ongoing Middle East conflict is pushing up energy costs. Higher oil prices act like a tax on households and businesses, squeezing spending further.

stories.title: Labor MPs asked to fund campaign to salvage budget
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports Labor MPs are being asked to help fund a campaign to 'salvage the budget' — a sign the government is feeling pressure on its fiscal position. With economic growth slowing and spending commitments piling up, the budget outlook is tighter than expected. No specific dollar figures were available in the headline data, but the political optics are uncomfortable heading into the second half of 2026.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Trump's new executive order creating a voluntary pre-check system for the major AI labs. Separately, Microsoft is making moves to reduce its reliance on OpenAI, and a prominent analyst has fired a warning shot at Google's AI strategy.

stories.title: Trump signs executive order for voluntary AI model pre-checks
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has created a system where AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic can voluntarily submit their new AI models for government review before launch. Crucially, this is not mandatory regulation — companies can opt in but don't have to. Critics argue this is a toothless compromise that satisfies neither safety advocates nor those worried about US-China AI competition. For investors, less regulation means fewer barriers to AI product launches — a mild positive for GOOG and MSFT.

stories.title: Microsoft unveils new AI models to reduce reliance on OpenAI
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft has released a new family of its own AI models specifically designed so developers don't have to rely on — or pay for — OpenAI's models. This is a smart strategic move: it lowers costs for developers building on Microsoft's platform and reduces Microsoft's own dependency on OpenAI (in which it has invested heavily but doesn't fully control). It also signals Microsoft wants to own more of the AI value chain itself, which is positive for long-term margins.

stories.title: Analyst warns Google is falling behind in AI — could be 'company-destroying'
stories.why_it_matters: Tech commentator M.G. Siegler has published a sharp critique arguing Google is now lagging behind both OpenAI and Anthropic in the AI race. His key concern: the shift to standalone AI apps (like ChatGPT) is eroding Google's core Search business, and Google hasn't responded decisively enough. He called some missteps potentially 'company-destroying' — strong language that spooked the market. For GOOG holders, this is a story to watch, though Google's fundamentals and AI infrastructure investment remain substantial.

stories.title: AI tools are reshaping software engineering — the industry is figuring out what's next
stories.why_it_matters: Business Insider reports that AI coding tools have triggered a genuine revolution in software development — code is being written faster than ever, and the industry is now grappling with what that means for software engineers' jobs and value. The piece reflects a broader shift: AI isn't just a product feature anymore, it's changing entire professions. This is the structural tailwind behind your GXAI.AX holding — the demand for AI tools isn't slowing down.

sport.summary: NRL Round 14 kicks off tomorrow night, with the Broncos hosting the Titans at Suncorp on Saturday the highlight for Gold Coast fans. There's plenty of player movement drama across the competition, and Roosters fans are having a rough week with more departures.

stories.title: Third star player quits Sydney Roosters, signs with rival club
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters are bleeding talent, with a third high-profile player now heading to a rival club. NRL fans are divided on whether this is a rebuild or a collapse — the article notes the departures are fuelling debate about the club's direction. No specific player names were available in the headline data, but the pattern of exits is raising real questions about the Roosters' culture and list management heading into the second half of 2026.

stories.title: Tigers star issues shock warning: 'I'll never be loyal to a club' — Benji at centre
stories.why_it_matters: A Wests Tigers star has publicly declared he'll never be loyal to any club — a remarkable statement that puts coach Benji Marshall in an awkward spot right in Round 14 build-up. The Tigers host the Panthers on Sunday. The comment suggests the player is weighing up a move and isn't shy about it, which could become a distraction for the club.

stories.title: NRL mid-season report card: Fallers, risers and 'staggering reality' for one contender
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports has published mid-season grades for every NRL club, with one former title contender described as facing a 'staggering reality' about their season. The piece also reveals each club's top trade targets as the transfer window heats up. No article text was available, but if you follow the ladder closely, it's worth a read for a full picture of where each club sits at the halfway point.

stories.title: Wimbledon faces player revolt over prize money
stories.why_it_matters: Players are reportedly pushing back against Wimbledon over prize money levels, with a potential revolt brewing before the tournament begins. The French Open prize money dispute has emboldened players, and Wimbledon — despite being one of the richest sporting events in the world — is now in the crosshairs. John McEnroe has also weighed in angrily after Emma Raducanu suffered a setback in her Wimbledon preparations. The grass court season storylines are heating up.
